label: June 15–21
title: “The Battle Is the Lord’s” —  1 Samuel 17–18; 24–26; 2 Samuel 5

items.text: Even when faced with seemingly insurmountable challenges, like the Philistine giant Goliath, remember that the Lord can deliver us. David’s victory was not won by sword or spear, but by unwavering faith in the Lord, teaching us that 'the battle is the Lord’s.'

Your own life story is filled with Goliath-size challenges, but like David, you can overcome them by exercising faith in the Lord. Consider how He has helped you in the past and trust Him to guide you as He authors your story.

When forces of evil gather against the forces of good, it's easy to feel small and insignificant. David's example shows that even one person with faith in Christ can make a profound difference, inspiring hope and courage to face large, complex problems.

The story of David and Goliath demonstrates that spiritual battles are won not by physical might, but by faith and divine assistance. Rely on the Lord, and He will empower you to overcome obstacles that seem impossible.

True friendship, as exemplified by Jonathan’s love for David, reminds us of Jesus Christ. Observe the attitudes and actions of those around you, learning from their examples to cultivate Christlike devotion and loyalty in your own relationships.

As you study the scriptures, liken them to your own life by learning from the motivations and actions of individuals like David, Jonathan, and Saul. This practice helps us identify potential weaknesses and grow wiser from their experiences.

Pride can lead to downfall, while forgiveness and self-control are the sure paths to peace and healing. David, Abigail, and others in these accounts demonstrate varying degrees of Christlike poise; seek opportunities to show this poise in your own life.

Abigail’s actions in 1 Samuel 25 liken her to Jesus Christ through her wisdom and peacemaking efforts. Her example teaches us about the healing power of forgiveness and the beauty that can emerge from difficult circumstances.

Even after significant victories, challenges persist. The Lord can provide essential direction for overcoming ongoing problems. By seeking His guidance, we can navigate complex situations and find strength to continue the fight for righteousness.

The scriptures are filled with imperfect individuals whose faithful choices offer profound lessons. By open-heartedly studying their lives, including their mistakes, we can learn to be more wise and avoid repeating errors, strengthening our spiritual journey.
